result.title: What Are LLM Agents Actually Learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization Benchmarks?
result.summary: Recent work reports large gains for LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization. We measure the contributions of online optimization, retrievable task information, and permissive oracle landscapes. On PMO at 50 oracle calls, a GPT-4o mini agent's sum AUC falls from 14.44 to 4.85 after task names and curated reference compounds are hidden. An identity-blinded condition that states only the oracle form (e.g., similarity to a hidden reference) scores 5.39, while a deterministic retrieval-only baseline with no LLM reaches 12.16 (84% of the full agent). A full 23-task 2x2 ablation and a three-seed replication on eight tasks support this interpretation. On a protein-targeted benchmark with an AutoDock Vina composite oracle, a single-edit random walk is a strong lower bound; across three seeds it obtains composite 0.636 +/- 0.008 and docking improvement -1.11 +/- 0.04 kcal/mol. As a positive control, a retrieval-free population agent exceeds REINVENT at a matched 50-call AUC budget, with its strongest result at 100 calls. These results motivate two inexpensive sanity checks: retrieval-safe PMO prompts and a random-walk floor for docking-based optimization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在低预算分子优化基准上拆解 LLM agent 的增益来源：通过隐藏任务名与参考化合物、identity-blind 条件、无 LLM 的检索基线及 2x2 消融，发现大部分收益来自可检索的任务信息而非在线优化，并据此提出检索安全的 prompt 与随机游走下界两项检验。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉任务，但其“信息检索贡献 vs 在线计算贡献”的拆解思路与遮蔽、下界检验设计，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 推理是否真正贡献、而非依赖捷径或任务先验提供评价框架线索。
